messages:
Aisha: Noticed a weird p99 wobble for /v1/generate on the latency dashboard after we shifted routing weights last night. p50/p95 steady. Anyone dug in yet?
Luca: I saw it. spike ~21:14UTC. digging through route breakdowns shows the fallback route latency tail is much higher for a handful of tenants, and that seems to drive the rolled-up p99.
Theo: FYI console shows a single merged p99 value with no provenance. that makes on-call noisy. we should surface origin-level counts and maybe the per-origin p99s.
Aisha: Agreed. Two quick hypotheses: 1) t-digest merge skew where small-origin heavy tails move the merged 99th, 2) time-bucketing mismatch: dashboard queries by event_time but our rollups use ingest_time, letting late-arriving slow samples leak into adjacent windows.
Luca: reproduced locally: when fallback samples are delayed by ~20s and have a fat tail, merged p99 can jump 30-40% even though the primary route p99 is unchanged.
Theo: Short-term mitigation: show a tooltip on the endpoint percentile that lists origins and sample counts, e.g. "merged — origins: primary=85% (p99=420ms), fallback=15% (p99=1.8s)". that'd avoid false alarms.
Aisha: +1. Also add a small warning icon if an origin contributes >10% to p99 but <N samples overall.
Luca: Longer-term we should consider: sample-weighted merge adjustments, or reconstructing raw samples for p99 when total samples < threshold instead of merging t-digests. Another option: prefer event_time consistently through pipeline to avoid alignment bias.
Theo: Will file a ticket and propose UX text for the tooltip. also propose a rollout gating rule: if any route's p99 increases >20% in canary vs baseline, fail the rollout.
deploy-bot: Created INF-4488: "Investigate rollup p99 uplift and add origin provenance to dashboard" assigned to @Luca and @Theo. Canary gating proposal added to ticket.
Luca: I'll attach the repro queries and a small replay to INF-4488. quick query I used: `SELECT pctl(0.99, latency_ms) AS p99, count() FROM traces WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' BY route, origin WINDOW 1m` and then compared to the rollup.
Aisha: Thanks. If we can get the dashboard to surface origin counts + per-origin p99s and a one-line explainer about t-digest merges, we should reduce noisy pages while we choose a merge heuristic.
